input_text: This Mutual Non-Disclosure Agreement is entered into on March 1, 2026 by and between Northstar Analytics Inc. and Cedar Ridge Labs LLC. Each party may disclose Confidential Information solely for evaluating a potential commercial partnership. Confidential Information includes technical plans, product roadmaps, customer lists, pricing, and security architecture. Exclusions include information that is public, already known without duty of confidentiality, independently developed, or rightfully obtained from a third party. Receiving party shall protect Confidential Information using at least reasonable care and no less than the care used for its own similar information. Use is limited to evaluation purposes and disclosure is limited to employees and contractors with a need to know who are bound by equivalent obligations. Term of agreement is three years; confidentiality obligations survive for five years from disclosure, except trade secrets which remain protected as long as they qualify as trade secrets. Compelled disclosure is permitted if legally required after prompt notice to disclosing party where lawful. Upon written request, recipient must return or destroy Confidential Information within 30 days, with one archival copy for legal compliance. No license is granted by implication. Injunctive relief is available for breach. Governing law is Delaware.
expected_summary: Mutual NDA between Northstar Analytics and Cedar Ridge Labs for evaluating a partnership. Confidential information is broadly defined, with standard exclusions (public, prior known, independently developed, third-party lawful source). Information may be used only for evaluation and shared only with bound personnel on a need-to-know basis. Agreement term is 3 years; confidentiality lasts 5 years from each disclosure, with trade secret protection continuing while legally protected. Legal compelled disclosure is allowed with notice where lawful. Recipient must return or destroy information within 30 days on request, retaining one compliance archive copy. Delaware law applies; injunctive relief and no implied license are included.
risk_flags: Trade secret survival is indefinite; ensure this is acceptable.
Archival copy exception should align with security and retention policies.

input_text: This Master Services Agreement governs consulting services by Iron Peak Consulting LLC for Harborline Health Systems. Statements of Work define scope, milestones, and fees. Client will pay undisputed invoices within 30 days; late payments accrue 1.0% monthly interest. Consultant warrants services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner for 30 days after delivery. Except for the foregoing warranty, services are provided as-is. Liability is limited to fees paid under the applicable SOW in the preceding 12 months, excluding liability for confidentiality breaches, gross negligence, willful misconduct, and indemnity obligations. Consultant indemnifies client for third-party claims alleging consultant deliverables infringe IP rights, subject to prompt notice and control of defense. Client indemnifies consultant for claims arising from client materials. Either party may terminate for material breach not cured within 15 days of notice; client may terminate for convenience with 30 days notice and payment for work performed. Consultant assigns work product IP to client upon full payment, excluding pre-existing materials and general know-how. Governing law is California.
expected_summary: MSA for consulting services with SOW-based scope and pricing. Invoices are due in 30 days; late payments accrue 1% monthly. Consultant provides a 30-day performance warranty, otherwise services are as-is. Liability is capped at fees paid in prior 12 months under the relevant SOW, with carve-outs for confidentiality, gross negligence, willful misconduct, and indemnities. Mutual indemnities allocate IP infringement risk to consultant deliverables and client-material claims to client. Termination includes material breach cure (15 days) and client convenience termination (30 days) with payment for completed work. Work product IP transfers to client after full payment, excluding consultant pre-existing IP and know-how. California law governs.
risk_flags: As-is disclaimer may be too broad for regulated healthcare work.
Convenience termination should define wind-down obligations and transition support.

input_text: Employee is hired as Senior Product Counsel at MetroLex Technologies starting April 15, 2026 with annual salary of 210,000 USD and eligibility for bonus up to 20%. Employment is at-will. Employee must comply with company policies including confidentiality and acceptable use. Company may terminate employment at any time with or without cause, subject to applicable law. If terminated without cause, employee receives 8 weeks severance conditioned on signing a release. Employee assigns to company inventions conceived or reduced to practice during employment related to company business. Employee agrees to a 12-month non-solicitation of employees and customers after termination. Non-compete provision restricts employee from working for a direct competitor in the US for 12 months post-termination. Disputes are subject to confidential arbitration in New York County. Agreement contains merger clause and may be amended only in writing signed by both parties.
expected_summary: Employment agreement for Senior Product Counsel at $210,000 salary plus up to 20% bonus, with at-will employment terms. Company can terminate anytime (subject to law); employee gets 8 weeks severance for without-cause termination if they sign a release. Employee must follow policies, maintain confidentiality, and assign relevant inventions. Post-employment restrictions include 12-month non-solicitation and a 12-month nationwide non-compete. Disputes go to confidential arbitration in New York County, and amendments require signed writing.
risk_flags: US-wide 12-month non-compete may be unenforceable or high risk in some jurisdictions.
Arbitration clause should address fee allocation and carve-outs for injunctive relief.

input_text: We collect personal information including name, email, billing details, usage logs, and device identifiers when users create accounts, purchase subscriptions, and interact with our platform. We use this data to provide services, process payments, secure systems, improve features, and communicate updates. We may share data with service providers for hosting, analytics, payment processing, and customer support under contractual restrictions. We retain personal data for as long as necessary to provide services, comply with legal obligations, resolve disputes, and enforce agreements. Users may request access, correction, deletion, or export of their personal information, subject to verification and legal exceptions. We use cookies and similar technologies to maintain sessions and understand product usage. International transfers may occur with safeguards such as standard contractual clauses. We implement technical and organizational security measures but cannot guarantee absolute security. We may update this policy and will post the revised date.
expected_summary: Policy describes collection of account, billing, usage, and device data for service delivery, payment, security, product improvement, and communications. Data sharing is limited to contracted vendors (hosting, analytics, payments, support). Retention is based on operational and legal needs. Users can request access, correction, deletion, and export, subject to verification and legal limits. Cookies are used for sessions and analytics. International transfers use safeguards such as SCCs. Security controls are implemented but not guaranteed. Policy may be updated with revised-date notice.
risk_flags: Retention language is broad; recommend defined retention schedules by data class.
Cross-border transfer disclosures should map to specific jurisdictions and mechanisms.
